validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence/classification. This is one of the most heavily documented pipelines in the tracker (the 'Bratstvo'/Brotherhood system's flagship trunk) — real, correctly classified as a gas transmission trunk. Not a duplicate of anything else on the roster: P0774 (Progress) is a genuinely separate, parallel trunk from a different origin field (Yamburg, not Urengoy), part of the same Brotherhood system but physically distinct pipe. See separate attribution and spec flags below.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently well beyond GEM/gem.wiki. The European Investment Bank's own project register (eib.org/en/projects/pipelines/all/20100598) documents a real EUR 150m EIB loan (signed 1/12/2014, total project cost EUR 355m) to PJSC Ukrtransgas for rehabilitation of 119 km of the Ukrainian section plus two compressor units, with Environmental and Social Impact Assessments filed through 2019 — an independent international financial institution financing physical repair works on this exact pipeline is about as strong existence evidence as this project gets. Independently, en.wikipedia.org's dedicated article and offshore-technology.com's pipeline database both describe the same physical asset: Urengoy gas field (Yamalo-Nenets AO, Russia) to Uzhhorod (Zakarpattia Oblast, Ukraine), part of a transit corridor onward to Slovakia/Central Europe. CLASSIFICATION: correct as a large-diameter (56in/1420mm) international gas transmission trunk — not a gathering/feeder line. STATUS caveat: the Gazprom-Naftogaz transit contract lapsed unrenewed on 2025-01-01 (RFE/RL, 2025), ending Russian-sourced transit flow through this corridor specifically (this was the pipeline's historical primary function) — this is dated evidence about THIS line, not a generic country-wide inference. Per the country-scope guidance this does NOT justify changing Status: Ukraine's GTS (including this trunk's Ukrainian section) continues in service for domestic transmission/storage cycling, and I found no dated evidence the physical Ukrainian section itself has been taken out of service. Recommend Update record the 2025-01-01 transit cessation in ResearcherNotes as a deliberate, sourced caveat rather than changing Status.

validity.recommendation: Revise the ownership split on the operators_owners tab. Owner1='Gazprom PJSC' at '100.00%' is wrong as written — Gazprom does not own the ~1,160 km Ukrainian section (per en.wikipedia). Recommend splitting Owner1=Gazprom PJSC (Russian section only, with a note that % applies to that section, not the whole pipe) and Owner2=Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine / its asset-holding parent (Ukrainian section; 100% Ukrainian-state-owned), rather than showing Gazprom at 100% with GTSOU as an unpercentaged afterthought.
validity.researcher_notes: This is a cross-border pipeline (Russia->Ukraine), so the country rule 'a wholly-Ukrainian row showing Gazprom ownership is a concern' doesn't apply literally — but the CURRENT sheet value goes further and wrong: Owner1%='100.00%' attached to Gazprom PJSC asserts Gazprom owns the entire pipeline, which is independently contradicted. Three independent sources confirm the Ukrainian section is Ukrainian-state property, not Gazprom's: (1) the EIB project page names the 2014 loan's promoter/financial intermediary as 'PJSC UKRTRANSGAS' (the pre-2020 Ukrainian state operator, a Naftogaz subsidiary) for rehab of the Ukrainian section specifically; (2) en.wikipedia.org's pipeline article states outright 'Russian section: Gazprom / Ukrainian section: UkrTransGaz' — i.e. two separate national owners/operators, not one; (3) en.wikipedia.org's Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine article and intellinews.com's 2020 unbundling piece both confirm GTSOU (UkrTransGaz's post-2020-01-01 successor as certified GTS operator) is wholly state-owned (via Mahistralni Gazoprovody Ukrainy/MGU, itself 100% held by the Ministry of Finance, then transferred to the Ministry of Energy) with Gazprom holding no stake in the Ukrainian GTS assets at all. The current Operator field ('Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine, Gazprom') is a reasonable description of the split-by-segment reality and I did not flag it; it is the Owner1 100% figure specifically that is unsupported.

validity.recommendation: Do not treat StartYear1=1983 as settled without a primary-source check. Two independent English-language sources (offshore-technology.com, en.wikipedia.org) both give 1984 as the commissioning year, not 1983. Recommend Update verify against a primary Gazprom/Soviet construction record (the gem.wiki page's own cited Gazprom Proektirovanie encyclopaedia page and the Batalin history page were both unreachable from this network — proektirovanie.gazprom.ru and gazprom.ru connections timed out — so I could not check GEM's likely original source directly) before changing the value either way.
validity.researcher_notes: offshore-technology.com states 'started operations in 1984'; en.wikipedia.org's current article states 'Construction: 1982-1984' and 'Commissioned: 1984'. Both are independent of each other and of gem.wiki, and they agree with each other against the sheet's 1983. Notably, an older mirrored snapshot of what appears to be a prior Wikipedia revision (via an ipfs.io cache) instead read 1983 — so even Wikipedia's own article text has been inconsistent on this specific point over time, which argues for genuine ambiguity in the underlying record (likely a 'first gas / construction substantially complete' date of 1983 vs. a 'full system commissioning' date of 1984, a common conflation for Soviet megaprojects with staged completion) rather than a clean GEM-is-wrong verdict. Flagging as a material spec disagreement per the corroboration rule (2 independent sources vs. the sheet) without proposing a specific replacement value.

fills.researcher_notes: EIB's project filings (through the 2019 Stakeholder Engagement Plan) describe an in-service asset undergoing safety/efficiency rehabilitation, not a decommissioned one. RFE/RL's 2025-01-01 report confirms the pipeline was actively carrying transit gas right up to the contract's expiry that day, and frames the change as a contractual/policy halt to transit flow, not a physical shutdown of the line. Status=operating is correct; the 2025-01-01 transit-flow cessation is a caveat, recorded in validity[] above, not a status change.
Both sources unambiguously describe a natural-gas pipeline moving gas from the Urengoy field; Fuel=Gas is correct.

56in/1420mm long-distance international trunk explicitly part of Ukraine's gas transmission system (EIB: 'Energy - Transportation and storage'; Wikipedia: transit corridor to Central/Western Europe) — transmission is correct, not a gathering/process/feeder line.

Could not independently corroborate 1983 specifically. Two independent English sources (offshore-technology.com, en.wikipedia.org) both give 1984 for commissioning. See the spec concern in validity[] above; leaving unresolved rather than citing sources that actually support a different year, and rather than proposing a change without checking a primary Gazprom/Soviet construction record (unreachable from this network).

en.wikipedia.org states the original design capacity as '32 billion cubic metres (1.1 trillion cubic feet) of natural gas per year', matching the sheet exactly. This is only a single independently-verified source (the Gazprom/gazpromexport.ru pages gem.wiki cites for this figure were unreachable — connection timeouts to gazprom.ru and gazpromexport.ru from this network on repeated attempts), so tier is medium, not high, pending a second source. Note the same Wikipedia article separately states throughput had fallen to ~27.9 bcm/y by 2009 — that is a utilisation figure, not a design-capacity revision, and does not conflict with Capacity=32.00 as a nameplate value.

offshore-technology.com states the length as exactly '4,451 km', matching the sheet precisely. en.wikipedia.org independently corroborates with a rounded '4,500 km (2,800 mi)' and additionally itemizes the Ukrainian section at 1,160 km — consistent, not conflicting (rounding of the same total).

Both independent sources agree on the primary 56in/1420mm diameter. Neither source states a secondary 1400mm figure; that value is plausible (some sections of large Soviet trunks of this era were laid in 1400mm pipe before 1420mm became the standard) but I found no independent confirmation of it specifically for this pipeline, so tier is medium (the 1420mm half is solidly corroborated, the 1400mm half is not independently verified either way — not flagged as wrong, just unconfirmed).
Both independent sources name the Urengoy gas field (Yamalo-Nenets AO, Siberia) as the pipeline's origin/source field.

All three independent sources agree: origin in the Urengoy field, Yamalo-Nenets AO, Russia; terminus at Uzhhorod, Zakarpattia Oblast, Ukraine (offshore-technology.com and EIB both use this exact start/end pairing).

fills.researcher_notes: en.wikipedia.org states outright: Russian section operated by Gazprom, Ukrainian section by UkrTransGaz. UkrTransGaz is the pre-2020 predecessor entity; GTSOU (Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine) is its certified successor as sole GTS operator since 2020-01-01 (per en.wikipedia's GTSOU article and intellinews.com's 2020 unbundling report, both cited in the attribution concern above) — so the current Operator value naming GTSOU + Gazprom correctly reflects the two-national-segments-two-operators reality, just phrased with the current (post-2020) name for the Ukrainian side, which is correct and consistent with country-wide convention. The EIB project page independently corroborates the Ukrainian-side operator lineage (naming 'PJSC Ukrtransgas' as the 2014 loan promoter for the Ukrainian section).

summary: P0768 (Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod, the Bratstvo/Brotherhood system's flagship trunk) is real, correctly classified, and not a duplicate — confirmed via EIB project financing records, en.wikipedia.org, and offshore-technology.com (length 4,451km and diameter 1420mm match exactly; capacity 32bcm/y single-sourced at medium tier). Two concerns: Owner1='Gazprom PJSC' at 100% is an ATTRIBUTION error (independent sources confirm the ~1,160km Ukrainian section is state-owned via GTSOU/MGU, not Gazprom's), left UNRESOLVED rather than confirmed; and StartYear1=1983 is a SPEC disagreement against two independent sources both giving 1984.
